target_customer: Small and medium sized employers who want to offer a 401(k) to their workers
problem: Small businesses find traditional 401(k) plans expensive and complex, so many workers have no workplace retirement plan.
business_model: B2B SaaS and recordkeeping fees paid by employers, plus asset-based fees (per general description; not verified in sources opened)
product_category: Fintech, small business 401(k) and retirement plans

founders.name: Roger Lee
previous_startups: Layoffs.fyi (per TechCrunch-linked mention in search results, secondary)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO. Education and prior employers not found in sources opened.

founders.name: Paul Sawaya
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO and says he now works on something new in gaming.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed integration with payroll providers, custodians and recordkeeping plus compliance workflows, which is standard fintech engineering with regulatory hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Plan administration and payroll integrations create switching costs once employers adopt, but several well-funded rivals pursued the same segment.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy it; a 2020 InvestmentNews article describes many new entrants in a race for small business 401(k)s, and Human Interest kept raising rounds through 2024.

market_need_then: Small employers lacked affordable plans, a gap the 2015 YC page positions as the core pain. No dated 2015 spend or regulation data was opened.

branding.name_origin: Originally Captain401, a name that implied focus on the 401(k); renamed Human Interest in February 2018 tied to giving small businesses access to a 401(k) (TechCrunch). No source gives the deeper reasoning.
branding.domain_note: Uses humaninterest.com; domain history not found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened

branding.brand_signature: A financial pun name, Human Interest, replacing the earlier Captain401

rebrands.why: Announced with the Series A; TechCrunch ties the new name to its goal for small business 401(k) access

brand_strength.rationale: The renamed brand supported a unicorn raise and large customer count (47,000 plus businesses per company site), but no source ties growth to the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Human Interest rebranded from Captain401 in 2018, raised $11M Series A, then scaled quickly: a $55M Series C and a $200M round at a $1B valuation in 2021, and a $267M round at $1.33B in July 2024. Its company site reports 47,000 plus business customers. The CEO has said it is preparing for an IPO, and no exit has occurred.
notes: TechCrunch 2021 states total raised $336.7M including $305M in the prior year. The round label for the August 2021 round is not stated by TechCrunch; the YC page and Otta call it Series D. Aggregators list a $3.5M seed (Feb 2016), a Series B of about $15.4M (Aug 2019), a 2025 $50M round and a reported 2025 valuation near $3B; all unverified and not recorded. Series C amount conflict: a trade article says a $105M Series C led by Glynn Capital. 2018 TechCrunch article names Money Intel as a rival but it is dated years after the batch so no competitor is listed. Founder education and employers not found.
